title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Fiduciary Duty - Receiving Gifts
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: After winning a complex LTB case, a deeply grateful client insists on giving the paralegal a $10,000 Rolex watch as a "thank you" gift, separate from the legal fees paid. Should the paralegal accept this gift?
options: Yes, gifts are unconditionally permitted as they are a sign of good client relations.
No, a paralegal must decline a significant or disproportionate gift unless the client has received independent legal advice, due to the fiduciary nature of the relationship.
Yes, but the paralegal must report the value of the watch as income to the LSO.
No, paralegals are entirely prohibited from receiving any gifts, even of nominal value, from clients.
questions.explain: Rule 3.06 (Transactions with Clients). Because of the power imbalance and fiduciary duty, accepting a substantial gift from a client raises concerns of undue influence. The paralegal should decline a significant gift unless the client has had independent legal advice. Nominal gifts (like a box of chocolates) are permissible.
